battle.name: 第二次達契亞戰爭
battle.theater: 多瑙河北岸塔帕埃山區
battle.brief: 公元105年達契亞王德凱巴魯斯趁圖拉真東征安息之機越過多瑙河、襲擊摩西亞，圖拉真回師建德羅貝塔石橋渡河，於105年冬與106年兩戰塔帕埃山隘，攻陷首都薩爾米澤蓋圖薩，德凱巴魯斯自盡，行省達契亞建立。卡面這件秦連弩並不在場，其西方同類是圖拉真紀功柱上所刻的車載弩砲。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的兩方是羅馬帝國與達契亞王國。羅馬方面，圖拉真在元老院授權下親自統率遠征，兵源取自多瑙河行省摩西亞上、下兩區的駐軍、帝國常備軍團、意大利與敘利亞抽調的輔助軍，以及各行省的騎兵與多瑙河艦隊；前線由圖拉真與其參謀將領分擔，多瑙河防務由摩西亞兩區的總督（legatus Augusti pro praetore）負責，編制上以重裝步兵大隊為中堅，輔助步兵營每營約五百人、輔助騎兵營約三百至五百人、騎兵大隊約五百人，工匠（fabri）隊擔任築營修路。達契亞方面是喀爾巴阡山中的部落聯盟王國，由「rex」德凱巴魯斯以宗教與軍事雙重權威統合；其國家結構以山中的堡壘、祭祀中心薩爾米澤蓋圖薩與各氏族自備的武裝為骨架，重裝步兵持長矛與鐮形彎刀，配以投石手、弓手與輕重騎兵，旗幟為狼頭的德魯科斯。公元101至102年的第一次達契亞戰爭後，達契亞僅餘北部山區的附庸地，德凱巴魯斯仍保有王的稱號與對金礦的支配，羅馬則在多瑙河南岸設下摩西亞總督區，並在德羅貝塔與卡皮達瓦修築邊防堡壘，試圖以這些據點封住對岸。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Roman Empire and the Kingdom of Dacia. On the Roman side Trajan commanded in person under the authority of the Senate, drawing his troops from the garrison of the two Danubian provinces of Moesia Superior and Moesia Inferior, from the standing legions of the imperial household, from auxiliary units drawn from Italy and Syria, and from the cavalry and the Danube fleet of the several provinces; the line was shared between Trajan himself and commanders such as Proculus, while the defence of the Danube was the responsibility of the two provincial governors of Moesia, and in the order of battle the legionary cohorts formed the centre, each auxiliary infantry cohort numbering about five hundred men, each auxiliary cavalry unit about three to five hundred, and the cavalry alae about five hundred apiece, with bodies of engineers (fabri) assigned to fort building and road making. On the Dacian side was a tribal confederacy in the Carpathian mountains, held together by a rex, Decebalus, through religious as well as military authority; the state rested on the hill forts, on the cult centre of Sarmizegetusa, and on the armed households of the clans, with heavy infantry carrying long spears and the curved falx, supported by slingers, archers, and light and heavy cavalry, and the wolf-headed draco for standard. After the First Dacian War of 101 to 102, Dacia had been reduced to a client realm in the northern highlands, where Decebalus kept the title of king and the control of the gold mines, while Rome created the province of the two Mossias on the southern bank of the Danube and raised frontier forts at Drobeta and Capidava to seal the opposite shore.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。羅馬方面是皇帝圖拉真（Marcus Ulpius Traianus），他於105至106年自敘利亞與安提阿返回歐洲，親自主持多瑙河戰線；未來的皇帝哈德良（Lucius Aelius Hadrianus）當時以第一敏神軍團（Legio I Minervia）軍團長身分在役，在第一次塔帕埃戰役中率領右翼縱隊，因地形失利一度陷入險境；圖拉真派往前線的多瑙河駐軍指揮官格奈烏斯·龐培·普羅庫魯斯負守土之責；工程師阿波羅多洛斯·達馬斯克（Apollodorus of Damascus）主持設計德羅貝塔的多瑙河石橋，橋墩分段沉入急流、以木構與斜撐加固，是羅馬橋樑工程的一次登峰之作；此戰最詳細的戰況記述出自卡西奧·狄奧（Marcus Cassius Dio）的《羅馬史》第六十八卷。達契亞方面是德凱巴魯斯（Decebalus），其名一般釋為「勇於決鬥者」，他在第一戰爭中曾被元老院當作人質帶往羅馬，返國即位後學會了羅馬式的謀略，也據此重整山區防禦；此外有兩名達契亞首領杜拉斯與德羅圖斯在戰局末段向羅馬投降，其侍從中有一人把短劍吞入腹中，寧死不作俘虜，成為狄奧筆下全戰最著名的一段插曲。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to the two sides. On the Roman side is the emperor Trajan (Marcus Ulpius Traianus), who returned from Syria and Antioch to Europe in 105 and 106 and personally directed the Danubian front; the future emperor Hadrian (Lucius Aelius Hadrianus), then commander of Legio I Minervia, was in the field and led the right-hand column in the First Battle of Tapae, where the ground cost him dearly and he was for a time in danger; Gnaeus Pompeius Proculus, whom Trajan had pushed forward to hold the Danube, was responsible for the defence of the soil already won; the engineer Apollodorus of Damascus designed the stone bridge of Drobeta, its piers set down in stages in the rapid water and braced with timber and struts, one of the high points of Roman bridge building; and the fullest account of the fighting comes from the sixty-eighth book of the History of Rome by Marcus Cassius Dio. On the Dacian side stands Decebalus, whose name is generally taken to mean the man who is brave in fight; he had been carried to Rome as a hostage by the Senate during the first war, and after returning to rule he learned the Roman way of fighting and reorganised the defence of the highlands on that model. Two further Dacian leaders, Duras and Drothus, surrendered to the Romans as the campaign ended, and among the servants of theirs was a man who swallowed his short sword, preferring death to captivity, which is the most famous episode in the whole of Dio's account.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是秦連弩：弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發，屬中國戰國末年至秦漢之際的連發弩機，見於《墨子》諸篇與《史記》所記的韓、趙連弩形制，矢匣儲箭、機括自閉，可連續射出，專為守城壓制攻城人流而設。它並沒有出現在多瑙河北岸的達契亞戰場上；同一技術譜系在羅馬的對應物是車載弩砲（carroballista）與手搖張弦的掌弩砲（cheiroballista），由維特魯維在《建築十書》第十卷描述其結構與操作人數，並被圖拉真紀功柱的浮雕生動記錄：弩身橫置於兩輪車上，弓臂以扭力儲能，箭匣順著機身排列，操作的士兵把箭矢推入機槽，工匠又在弩砲上搭起木板與獸皮頂棚，抵住從岩壁落下的石塊與火箭。羅馬全軍還配備投石機（onager）對付山堡城牆，皮洛投槍、大盾、短劍與騎槍構成近戰骨架，軍團工兵專司築營、築壘與掘壕；多瑙河艦隊以駁船運糧送兵，渡河則用狄奧記載的那座馬其頓式浮橋，橋身以鐵鏈相連、上面鋪板並覆以油布。達契亞方面以長矛、鐮刀、短弓、投石手與鎧甲騎兵為主，守壘時另有從羅馬人手中繳獲的弩砲與投石器可用。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Qin repeating crossbow: the lock stores the pull of the bow and sends an arrow with a stamp of the foot, a volley crossbow of the late Warring States and the Qin-Han period, described in the chapters of Mozi and in the accounts of the repeating crossbows of Han and Zhao in the Records of the Grand Historian, with a magazine of bolts, a self-closing trigger, and the capacity to fire in succession, made for the defence of walls against men coming up them. It did not appear on the field north of the Danube in Dacia. The counterpart in the same line of technology on the Roman side was the cart-mounted carroballista and the hand-cranked cheiroballista, whose construction and crew numbers are described by Vitruvius in the tenth book of his treatise on architecture, and which are vividly recorded in the reliefs of Trajan's Column: the engine lies across a two-wheeled cart, the bow arms store their energy in torsion, the bolts stand in rows along the frame, the crew push the bolts into the groove, and the engineers roof the machine over with planks and hides to keep off the stones and fire arrows thrown down from the rock. The Roman army also carried the onager for stone-throwing against the hill forts, and pilum, scutum, gladius and contus formed the framework of close combat, with the legionary engineers assigned to camps, redoubts and ditches. On the Danube, barges carried grain and men, and the river was crossed by the pontoon bridge in the Macedonian manner described by Dio, its sections joined with iron chains, planked over and covered with oiled hide. The Dacians fought with long spears, falx, short bows, slingers and armoured cavalry, and on their strongholds they had bolt-throwers and stone-throwers of their own, some of them taken from Roman soldiers.
tactics: 羅馬的戰術核心是分縱隊推進與攻城器械的壓制。渡過多瑙河之後，圖拉真把大軍分為左中右三路：右翼由哈德良率第一敏神軍團，中軍與左翼由圖拉真與普羅庫魯斯分領，騎兵遮蔽外側，工匠隊沿途築壘修路，形成可回頭防守的縱深。接近山區時，羅馬不再強行展開，改以縱隊前進：先鋒以盾牆護住弩砲，其後是標槍齊射區，再後是步兵主力，最後由工兵開路。遇上隘口與山堡，羅馬先用弩砲與投石機在遠處壓制城頭，然後以盾陣（testudo）護住進攻部隊接近牆根，攻城塔與梯子同時靠上去；圖拉真紀功柱上刻出的，正是弩砲頂棚下士兵操作弩機、敵方從岩壁投下石塊的場面。渡河與峽谷是另一道難題，狄奧記載羅馬在鐵門關一帶先用舟橋渡過急流，再以夜襲奪取阻塞河道、卡住隘口的堡壘。德凱巴魯斯的應對則是避免正面會戰：他不斷以游騎襲擊羅馬的工匠隊與後方輜重，用熟悉山道的鋒線兵在狹窄地形中分割敵軍縱隊，退守有水源的山堡，焚毀橋樑與穀倉，拖到羅馬主力在山區受寒受飢、糧道拉長時再尋機反擊。
tacticsEn: The core of the Roman method was the advance in separate columns and the pressure of the siege engines. Once over the Danube, Trajan divided the army into three: the right wing under Hadrian with Legio I Minervia, the centre and the left under Trajan and Proculus between them, the cavalry screening the outer flanks, and the engineers building redoubts and roads as they marched, so that a defensible depth grew behind them. On approaching the mountains the Romans no longer tried to deploy in line but formed up in column: an advance guard covered the bolt-throwers behind a wall of shields, behind that the zone of the pilum volley, behind that the main body of infantry, and last of all the engineers to open the road. At a defile or a hill fort the Romans first silenced the ramparts from a distance with bolt-throwers and stone-throwers, then brought the assault up under the testudo, with siege towers and ladders going in at the same time; what the Column of Trajan shows is exactly the machine under its timber and hide roof while the enemy throws stones down from the rock. Crossing the river and the gorges were the other difficulty, for Dio records how the Romans first passed the rapids on boats in the Iron Gates and then took by night the fort that blocked the channel and the pass. Decebalus answered by refusing to be drawn into a set-piece battle: he harried the Roman engineers and the baggage train with raiding parties, used the troops who knew the mountain paths to cut the Roman columns apart in the narrow ground, fell back on the forts that held water, burned the bridges and the granaries, and waited for the moment when the Roman main body, cold and hungry in the mountains and stretched along a long supply line, would have to turn and fight.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。戰爭自公元105年達契亞人越過多瑙河襲擊摩西亞起，至106年薩爾米澤蓋圖薩陷落、德凱巴魯斯身亡止，前後約兩年。羅馬的德羅貝塔石橋建於105年，全長約一千一百三十五公尺、寬約二十公尺，以二十個石基分段落水，戰後不久被毀，117年圖拉真再戰時改以浮橋越河。德羅貝塔至薩爾米澤蓋圖薩的山道約兩百五十公里，中途穿過鐵門關峽谷，關內的塔布拉·特拉亞納碑刻記下自鐵門關起算的里程，並署中央百夫長普羅庫魯斯·馬克西穆斯（centurio Proculus Maximus）之名，是這條道路開鑿的見證。兵員方面，古代文獻沒有留下羅軍確數，現代史家一般估計圖拉真投入達契亞的野戰部隊為數萬人，帝國常備軍團總數在三十個上下；征服後行省的駐軍以第十三合流軍團（Legio XIII Gemina）為骨幹，總量約相當於十餘個軍團。金錢方面，新行省繼承達契亞金礦，羅馬在阿爾布魯斯·馬約爾一帶開採金銀，長期供應造幣。圖拉真紀功柱則是一根高五米五、底徑三米七、盤繞二十段浮雕的巨型大理石柱，113年才在圖拉真廣場落成，柱上浮雕把兩次達契亞戰爭的場面一一刻出，成為今日最可靠的裝備與編制圖證。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war began in 105, when the Dacians crossed the Danube and raided Moesia, and ended in 106 with the fall of Sarmizegetusa and the death of Decebalus, so it lasted about two years. The stone bridge at Drobeta was built in 105; it was about 1,135 metres long and some 20 metres wide, set on twenty stone piers stepped down into the water, and it was destroyed not long after the war, so that in 117 Trajan crossed the river on a pontoon bridge instead. The mountain road from Drobeta to Sarmizegetusa was about 250 kilometres and passed through the gorges of the Iron Gates, where the Tabula Traiana records the distance reckoned from the Gates and carries the name of the centurion Proculus Maximus, the witness of the cutting of that road. On troops, the ancient sources give no exact figure for the Roman army; modern historians generally put the field force Trajan committed in Dacia at a number of tens of thousands, with about thirty legions in the imperial standing army as a whole, and the garrison left in the province after the conquest had the XIII Gemina as its backbone, in an establishment of the order of a dozen legions. As to money, the new province inherited the Dacian gold mines, and Rome worked gold and silver around Alburnus Maior for a long time to feed the mint. The Column of Trajan is a marble shaft five and a half metres high and 3.7 metres in diameter, with twenty spiral bands of relief, and it was not erected in the Forum of Trajan until 113; its carvings put the scenes of both Dacian wars on record and remain the surest evidence we have for the equipment and the order of battle of the age.
cause: 這場戰爭是第一次達契亞戰爭（101至102年）的直接後果。那一場戰爭裡，圖拉真的羅軍攻入達契亞心腹，摧毀了首都薩爾米澤蓋圖薩的祭祀中心與大量財富，卻沒有能夠把整個山區國家連根拔起：德凱巴魯斯退守北部山區，作為羅馬附庸保留王的頭銜，控制的只剩下堡壘、峭壁與礦區。和平的條件因此極不對等——羅馬要求山區臣服並保證不再襲擊邊境，達契亞則需要礦產收入、鹽源與不被羅馬扶植的貴族瓜分。105年圖拉真東征安息、多瑙河前線只剩守備薄弱的摩西亞行省時，德凱巴魯斯抓住這個空檔率軍越過多瑙河，攻破下摩西亞總督的陣營並致其陣亡，隨後反覆襲擾邊境，摧毀羅馬在德羅貝塔與卡皮達瓦一線的堡壘與糧道，試圖用戰爭把羅馬重新拖回談判桌。他原本還打算在羅馬扶植的附庸地區策反，藉內應打開通往多瑙河南岸的路。對圖拉真而言，黃金本身並非首要理由，但達契亞山區一旦陷落，羅馬就能同時掌握多瑙河的門戶、班諾特與特蘭西瓦尼亞的礦藏，以及通往黑海與多瑙河口的地理縱深；而不能容忍的，則是前線總督陣亡這件事本身所代表的恥辱。
causeEn: This war was the direct consequence of the First Dacian War of 101 to 102. In that war Trajan's Romans struck into the heart of Dacia, destroyed the cult centre of the capital Sarmizegetusa and a great deal of the wealth of the country, but could not root the whole mountain state out of the ground: Decebalus fell back into the northern highlands and, as a Roman client, kept the title of king, with nothing left to hold but forts, cliffs and mines. The terms of the peace were therefore grossly unequal. Rome required submission from the highlands and a promise that the raids across the river would not be repeated; Dacia needed the revenue of its mines, its salt, and freedom from being carved up by the Roman party of clients. In 105, while Trajan was in the East against Parthia and the Danubian front was held by the thin garrison of the province of Moesia, Decebalus seized the opening, led his troops over the Danube, broke the camp of the governor of Lower Moesia and killed him, and then harried the frontier again and again, destroying the Roman forts and supply lines along the line of Drobeta and Capidava, in the hope of dragging Rome back to the negotiating table by force of arms. He also meant to raise trouble among the client communities planted by Rome, and to open a road back to the southern bank from within. For Trajan the gold was hardly the first consideration, but if the Dacian highlands fell, Rome would hold at one time the gate of the Danube, the mines of Banat and Transylvania, and the geographical depth that ran on towards the Black Sea and the mouths of the river; and what could not be tolerated at all was the humiliation represented by the death of a provincial governor on his own front.
impact: 達契亞的陷落改變了地中海世界的權力地圖。106至107年間，羅馬在達契亞設立行省，以舊王都附近的烏爾皮亞·特拉亞納·薩爾米澤蓋圖薩為省治，安置移民、劃分土地，並在礦區設立財政代理人，開始把達契亞黃金大量送進造幣廠；然而同時，帝國也背上了高昂的代價——大批達契亞人淪為奴隸或被強行遷往行省各地，喀爾巴阡山脈成為羅馬的新邊界，羅馬不得不在多瑙河與山脈之間維持一條漫長而脆弱的接觸線，與北方森林中的魯克索拉尼人、塞維里人接壤。圖拉真本人因此獲得「達契亞的凱旋者」稱號，並在圖拉真廣場建起圖書館、烏爾皮亞大殿與那根把戰役全程刻入石中的紀功柱，廣場的公共工程本身就靠達契亞黃金支付。卡面這件秦連弩在這一幕裡的位置，是作為技術對照：它在中國與地中海兩個世界各自走完了「把拉力存起來、再連續放出」的同一條路，而在多瑙河北岸，真正壓制山堡的是羅馬的車載弩砲與投石機——金屬車架、扭力弓臂、箭匣順排，這種可連發的弩砲在圖拉真紀功柱上被雕得清清楚楚。
impactEn: The fall of Dacia redrew the political map of the Mediterranean world. Between 106 and 107 Rome set up the province of Dacia, made Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa near the old royal capital its administrative seat, settled colonists, surveyed the land, and appointed fiscal agents to the mines, and began to send great quantities of Dacian gold into the mint. At the same time the empire took on a heavy bill: great numbers of Dacians were enslaved or forcibly moved to the provinces, the Carpathians became the new frontier of Rome, and Rome had to hold a long and fragile line of contact between the Danube and the mountains, touching the Roxolani and the Siraces in the northern forests. Trajan himself took the title of Dacicus, conqueror of Dacia, and raised in his forum a library, the Basilica Ulpia, and that column which carved the whole of the campaign into stone, the public works of the square itself being paid for out of the Dacian gold. The place of the Qin repeating crossbow in this scene is that of a technical parallel: in China and in the Mediterranean it had walked the same road of storing the pull of the bow and letting it go again in succession, and what really pinned the hill forts on the north bank of the Danube was the Roman carroballista and the stone-thrower, with its iron frame, its torsion arms and its rowed magazine of bolts, carved on the Column of Trajan so plainly that the machine can still be read from the relief.
result: 結果是達契亞的獨立就此終結。德凱巴魯斯在薩爾米澤蓋圖薩陷落後向北逃亡，退入喀爾巴阡山深處，最後在山中堡壘被羅馬騎兵包圍；據狄奧記載，他先殺死同行者以免對方落入羅馬手中，隨後自刃身亡，頭顱被送到圖拉真面前，圖拉真下令將它送回羅馬安葬。失去君主的達契亞人選擇了最決絕的收場：大批守軍在山堡中自相殘殺與自盡，僅少數向羅馬投降，狄奧記下的那個把短劍吞進腹中、寧死不作俘虜的侍從，成為這場戰爭最著名的註腳。羅馬則在廢墟上建立行省，鎮壓達契亞精英，拆毀聖所並取走祭祀器物，同時修復德羅貝塔的多瑙河通道，於圖拉真廣場立柱紀功。代價同樣記在帳上：喀爾巴阡山並未因此變得平坦，羅馬需要不斷派兵，而德凱巴魯斯之死所帶來的屈辱感，在隨後的歲月裡始終未被消化。史書把這場戰爭視為圖拉真一生最輝煌的成就，而卡牌上這位「一踩一發」的守城者，則在遙遠的東方與這場山岳戰爭共享同一個念頭：用一台能連發的弩機，把攻上來的人擋在牆外。
resultEn: The result was the end of Dacian independence. After the fall of Sarmizegetusa, Decebalus fled north into the depths of the Carpathians and was at last surrounded by Roman horsemen in a fort among the mountains; according to Dio he first killed the man who was with him so that the man should not fall into Roman hands, and then took his own life, and his head was carried to Trajan, who ordered that it be carried back to Rome for burial. The Dacians, with their king gone, chose the most desperate ending: great numbers of the garrisons of the hill forts killed each other and themselves, and only a few surrendered to the Romans, and that servant of Dio who swallowed his short sword rather than be taken alive has become the best known footnote to the whole war. Rome on its side set up the province among the ruins, put down the Dacian elite, pulled down the sanctuary and carried off its sacred vessels, at the same time repairing the crossing of the Danube at Drobeta, and set up the column in the forum to commemorate the campaign. The cost was entered in the ledger as well: the Carpathians did not become level ground because of it, Rome was left needing to send troops without end, and the humiliation carried by the death of Decebalus was never digested in the years that followed. The historians of Rome treat this war as the brightest achievement of Trajan's life, while the keeper of the wall on this card, the one who fires with a stamp of the foot in far-off China, shares with the mountain war the same simple idea: a crossbow that can fire in succession keeps the men coming up the wall outside it.
